label: lem-oscillation-characterisation-in-rn
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Checked empty, zero, one, degenerate, endpoint, nonempty-choice, and isolated-point cases; no counterexample found. The biconditional (continuity ⇔ ω_f(c)=0) holds exactly. The relative-closedness proof for bounded f is valid (the boundedness hypothesis is sufficient, though the argument works more generally). The only quickly closable gap is the implicit use of the triangle inequality to obtain B(d,r/2)⊆B(c,r); a competent reader fills it within seconds. All quantified statements are correctly discharged.

SOURCES: Inspected the full exact text of all six declared dependencies. def-metric-continuity and def-metric-ball supply the ε-δ and ball formulations of continuity. def-oscillation-in-rn provides the oscillation definition, the monotonicity of ω_f(⋅), and fixes the Euclidean metric. def-metric-topology defines relatively closed sets. lem-p-norms-are-norms-and-induce-the-published-metrics confirms the Euclidean metric is a metric. def-bounded-set supports the boundedness condition. Every load-bearing property used in the proof is explicitly present in these sources.

CHECKED: Confirmed title, full public Statement, Facts & Assumptions, every numbered proof step (1.1–2.1), and the absence of Remarks. The proof correctly derives the equivalence from L1 and L2, and the closedness of the superlevel set from the openness of the sublevel set. No fatal defect, missing hypothesis, or invalid inference was identified.
